attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, presented as his view.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps 'seemingly', 'every software product' and 'wants to add'. It is framed as an observation, but it is a hedged impression joined to a value judgment, so it cannot be tested.

contract.note: Calling it not adjudicable is fair. Whether vendors 'explained how it'll make anything better' is subjective, 'seemingly' marks an impression, and the speaker gave no measure.

evidence.note: Zoom's own September 2023 release shows a product he named adding AI and claiming productivity benefits in general terms. Whether that counts as explaining the benefit is a judgment, so this is context only.

reviews.rationale: The statement is a hedged impression ('seemingly') plus a judgment on whether vendors explained the benefits well enough. No objective measure exists. Zoom adding AI is the one checkable fact, and it does not test his point. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Zitron himself says the promise was 'yet to keep'. The Musk quote is a paraphrase used as background, and the scored part is Zitron's own claim.

semantics.note: Observation, as of the post date, that the self-driving promise had not been kept. Faithful.

contract.note: The plain reading (new Teslas still needed human supervision as of January 2024) is the ordinary reading. It is fair, and it does not depend on Musk's exact 2016 wording.

evidence.note: Archived Tesla support page from about January 2024: the features need active driver supervision and do not make the car autonomous. Company disclosure, against its own interest. The exact snapshot date is uncertain.
Tesla's December 2023 recall filing with NHTSA calls Autosteer SAE Level 2, with the driver as operator. It covers cars built through December 7, 2023. In the target period.
2016 report on the full self-driving hardware announcement. Background only; it does not show the 2024 status.
April 2025 CNBC report that Tesla still offered no unsupervised car. Outside the target period, so context only, even though the item labels it 'supports'.

reviews.rationale: Tesla's support page from about January 2024 and its December 2023 NHTSA filing both show its driving features needed active human supervision and were Level 2. The packet has no evidence of unsupervised driving by January 2024. The promise had not been kept as of the post. Supported.
